name: IceCube
summary: A cubic-kilometre observatory in South Pole ice that established the high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux and now studies its sources, neutrino properties and transient phenomena.
physics_targets: Indirect dark matter and exotic-particle searches
detection_principle: Digital optical modules measure the timing and brightness of Cherenkov light from charged particles produced in neutrino interactions. Tracks, cascades and tau signatures give complementary direction, energy and flavour information; DeepCore provides a denser low-energy region.

sites.name: Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station
sites.location: Antarctic ice at the geographic South Pole

status.label: Operating / data taking
status.evidence: The collaboration describes the existing observatory as operating and announced Upgrade deployment in February 2026.

timeline.event: Installation completed in December 2010; full detector science operation followed in 2011.
Discovery evidence for a high-energy astrophysical neutrino population published.
Upgrade deployment announced complete in February.
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics recognized Francis Halzen for contributions to IceCube and astrophysical-neutrino discoveries.

collaboration.name: IceCube Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Original in-ice array
key_parameters.value: 5,160 optical modules on 86 strings; approximately 1 km³

key_parameters.name: DeepCore
key_parameters.value: Densely instrumented internal array for atmospheric-neutrino measurements down to a few GeV

key_parameters.name: Upgrade
key_parameters.value: More than 600 new sensors and calibration devices deployed in 2025–2026; the collaboration February release describes five new strings

results.summary: A population of high-energy events inconsistent with atmospheric backgrounds established astrophysical neutrino detection.
Multimessenger studies, evidence for NGC 1068 emission and a Galactic-plane neutrino signal expanded the source programme.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
